finding_key: packages/backend/src/main.ts::rawbody capture keyed on an exact-string url match; any path variation (trailing slash, differing case, future global prefix) leaves `rawbody` undefined and the guard 401s every webhook
evidence: packages/backend/src/main.ts:51 does a literal `req.url?.split('?',1)[0] === '/internal/yorkie/events'` compare, and the constant is hand-duplicated from `@Controller('internal/yorkie')`/`@Post('events')` with no linkage. Express defaults are non-strict and case-insensitive routing, so `POST /internal/yorkie/events/` (or a case variant) still reaches the controller but skips the rawBody capture, after which yorkie-signature.guard.ts:49 (`if (!header || !rawBody)`) throws UnauthorizedException on every delivery — a silent 401/retry loop where `updatedAt` never advances. The claim's "future global prefix" variant is speculative (the supplied main.ts has no setGlobalPrefix), and the trailing-slash case requires an operator registering a URL that differs from the documented ops command, so I score it minor rather than major; it is real brittleness, untested, with a silent total-feature-failure mode.
